patch.objective: Teach a client on warfarin to keep vitamin K intake consistent, and know a higher INR means higher bleeding risk

sources.note: Relayed from the LPN/VN course's earlier cases (read 2026-11-11, primary PDF), not re-read for this band: the practical nursing course is built toward this test plan.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

Relayed from the NCLEX-PN case warfarin-inr-high-tarry-stool, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the REQ-233 NCLEX-PN cases (read 2026-11-11, primary PDF), not re-read: Coordinated Care includes care within the legal scope of practice; Physiological Adaptation includes recognizing and reporting a change in the client's condition.

sources.cite: MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine). Warfarin drug information (revised 2026-03-15)
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-PN case warfarin-inr-high-tarry-stool, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes: 'Warfarin may cause serious bleeding that can lead to death'; report 'pink, red, or dark brown urine, red or tarry black bowel movements, headache, dizziness, or weakness', frequent nosebleeds and bleeding gums; regular blood tests (INR) track the response; 'Eat consistent amounts of vitamin K-containing food on a week-to-week basis', avoiding large amounts of leafy green vegetables. No dose is used in the case.

Relayed from the NCLEX-PN case warfarin-inr-high-tarry-stool, not re-read for this band; its note: Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model. Disease courses, effect sizes and local waits are authored and carry FLAG.
